## Proof

Let $\{W(t)\mid t\ge 0\}$ be a standard Brownian motion. We want
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[W^{2}(4)\mid W(1),W(2)\right].$$

**Step 1: Decompose $W(4)$.** By the independent-increments property of Brownian motion,
$$W(4)=W(2)+\bigl(W(4)-W(2)\bigr).$$
The increment $W(4)-W(2)$ is independent of $\mathcal{F}_{2}=\sigma(W(s):0\le s\le 2)$, and in particular of $(W(1),W(2))$. Moreover,
$$W(4)-W(2)\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\,4-2)=\mathcal{N}(0,2).$$

**Step 2: Conditional distribution.** Conditioning on $(W(1),W(2))$ fixes $W(2)$ as a known constant and leaves $W(4)-W(2)$ unchanged in distribution (by independence). Hence, conditionally,
$$W(4)\mid W(1),W(2)\;=\;W(2)+Z,\qquad Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,2),\quad Z\perp\!\!\!\perp(W(1),W(2)).$$

**Step 3: Compute the second moment.** Using $\mathbb{E}[Z]=0$ and $\mathbb{E}[Z^{2}]=\operatorname{Var}(Z)=2$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[W^{2}(4)\mid W(1),W(2)\right]
&=\mathbb{E}\!\left[\bigl(W(2)+Z\bigr)^{2}\mid W(1),W(2)\right]\\
&=\mathbb{E}\!\left[W^{2}(2)+2W(2)Z+Z^{2}\mid W(1),W(2)\right]\\
&=W^{2}(2)+2W(2)\,\mathbb{E}[Z]+\mathbb{E}[Z^{2}]\\
&=W^{2}(2)+2W(2)\cdot 0+2\\
&=W^{2}(2)+2.
\end{aligned}
$$

**Result.**
$$\boxed{\mathbb{E}\!\left[W^{2}(4)\mid W(1),W(2)\right]=W^{2}(2)+2.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
